question.problem: Which of the following describes the level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡z}{x+y}?$
question.worked_solution:
The level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ \frac{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡z}{x+y} & =c \\ \operatorname{arcsin}⁡z & =c(x+y) \\ z & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(c(x+y))\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get a family of surfaces given by:

$$
z=\operatorname{sin}⁡(c(x+y)),\,c\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

A family of surfaces given by $z=\operatorname{cos}⁡(c(x+y))$
A family of surfaces given by $z=c\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)$
A family of surfaces given by $z=\operatorname{sin}⁡(c(x+y))$

responses.value: A family of surfaces given by $z=\operatorname{sin}⁡(c(x+y))$
